title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' that follow the Longue Marche. Grothendieck is working in genus 1, with the modular group SL2(Z) generated by two elliptic elements. rho = [[0,1],[-1,1]] has order 6 and sigma = [[0,1],[-1,0]] has order 4 (from the previous page). On that page he summarises ('Rétrospective') two group schemes over Z, with G = GL(2)_Z:
- M_{rho,sigma} = {(U,a,b)} with U in G, a in T_rho, b in N'_sigma, subject to det U = det b = eps' det a and eps'^2 = 1.
- SM_{rho,sigma} = B'_0 x_{G_m} M_{rho,sigma}, with an extra coordinate u in the 'ax+b' group B'_0 = {[[mu,lambda],[0,1]]}.
- The tori are T_rho = (Z[rho])^* (the norm torus of Z[zeta_3]) and T_sigma = (Z[sigma])^* (the norm torus of Z[i]).
- N'_sigma is the stabiliser of sigma up to sign. It is an extension of mu_2 by T_sigma.

This page.
- (12)-(13): the three structural homomorphisms Theta_G, Theta_rho, Theta_sigma are completed by three characters. These are chi = det∘Theta_G (to G_m), eps_2 = eps_sigma∘Theta_sigma (to mu_2) and eps_3 = det a / det b (to mu_2). Together they embed M_{rho,sigma} into G x T_rho x N'_sigma x G_m x mu_2 x mu_2.
- (14): the image is cut out by det U = det b = eps' det a = mu and by b sigma b^{-1} = eps sigma.
- (15)-(16): the same is done for SM_{rho,sigma}, which embeds into B'_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma x G x G_m x mu_2 x mu_2 via (u,a,b,U,mu,eps,eps').
- (17)-(18): a second, 'loop-equation' presentation is introduced:
  SΣ*_{rho,sigma} = {(alpha,beta,f,mu,eps) : (det alpha)^2 = det beta = det f = 1, alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} = eps · beta sigma(beta)^{-1} · eps_1^{mu-1}},
  where eps_1 = [[1,0],[1,1]] and eps_1(nu) = eps_1^nu = [[1,0],[nu,1]].

On the next page Grothendieck notes that the projection to (alpha,beta,f) is already a monomorphism. He gives an explicit isomorphism SM → SΣ* by alpha = u a^{-1}, beta = u b^{-1}, f = u U^{-1}. It is compatible with the action of L_0 = Ker(det on B'_0), and he passes to the quotient M ≅ Σ* = L_0\SΣ*. He then states canonical maps from (S_0)M~_{0,3}, the group attached to the Teichmüller-tower / loop-equation side, to M_{rho,sigma}(Ẑ)/Σ and SM_{rho,sigma}(Ẑ)/Σ.

Meaning. Read conjugation rho(x) = rho x rho^{-1}. Note that eps_1 = rho sigma^{-1}, so sigma^{-1} rho = [[1,-1],[0,1]] is the parabolic (cusp) generator. Substituting alpha = u a^{-1}, beta = u b^{-1} makes a and b disappear, because they centralise rho and normalise sigma up to sign. The equation in (17) then reduces to u (sigma^{-1}rho) u^{-1} = (sigma^{-1}rho)^mu. This is exactly satisfied by u = [[mu,lambda],[0,1]].

So (17) is the 2x2-matrix ('linear', congruence-level) shadow of the genus-1 loop equation. The images of the order-6 and order-4 generators are conjugates alpha rho alpha^{-1} and beta sigma beta^{-1}, up to the central sign eps. Their product is forced to be a conjugate of the cusp generator raised to the cyclotomic exponent mu = chi. This is the GL2/SL2 analogue of the Drinfeld–Ihara normalisation x ↦ x^lambda, y ↦ f^{-1} y^lambda f.

The point of the page is bookkeeping: to present the target group scheme in two equivalent ways ('torsor/normaliser' coordinates versus 'loop-equation' coordinates). That way the arithmetic/Teichmüller group can be mapped into its Ẑ-points.
errors: (14): 'b(sigma)=eps sigma i.e. sigma(b) = eps b i.e. b^t b = eps' is only correct for det b = 1. On GL2 one has sigma^{-1} b sigma = det(b)·(b^t)^{-1}, so the correct condition is b b^t = eps·det(b). Check: for b in T_sigma, b^t b = (t^2+u^2)·I = det b; for b = diag(1,-1), eps = -1 and det b = -1. The marginal note 'sigma(b) : t b^{-1}' tacitly drops the det factor.
(16): 'b(sigma) = eps(sigma)' is a slip for b sigma b^{-1} = eps·sigma.

(15): the factors are written B'_rho x T_sigma in the transcription. The previous page (2) has SM ⊂ B'_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma x G, so the first two factors should be B'_0 and T_rho, and the fourth should be G (written with an underline/correction).

(17): the sign bookkeeping between eps (from N'_sigma) and eps' (from det alpha = ±1) is not spelled out. The identity (det alpha)^2 = 1 holds because det alpha = mu/det a = eps', which is consistent.
The constraint on f (det f = 1 only) means the f-coordinate just carries a free SL2-factor (from U). This is not an error, but the loop equation does not involve f.

ideas.what: Group scheme over Z built from GL2, the tori of Z[zeta_3] and Z[i], and the normaliser of the order-4 torus, as a linear target for the genus-1 Teichmüller/GT-type group
ideas.modern_name: congruence (SL2(Ẑ)/GL2(Ẑ)) image of a genus-1 Grothendieck–Teichmüller group; normaliser-type group schemes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Genus-1 GT: Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997), Enriquez (elliptic associators, 2014); the action of GT on SL2(Ẑ) is folklore
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished notes (140-3); the Esquisse mentions the role of M_{1,1} and the elliptic elements of SL2(Z) only in passing

ideas.what: Twisted loop equation alpha rho alpha^{-1}rho^{-1} = eps beta sigma beta^{-1} sigma^{-1} eps_1^{mu-1}, encoding that the cusp generator sigma^{-1}rho goes to its mu-th power
ideas.modern_name: genus-1 analogue of the Drinfeld–Ihara relation for GT (cyclotomic normalisation at the cusp)

ideas.what: Equivalence of the 'torsor' coordinates (u,a,b,U) and the 'loop' coordinates (alpha,beta,f) via alpha = u a^{-1}, beta = u b^{-1}, f = u U^{-1}, with quotient by L_0
ideas.modern_name: change of variables / torsor trivialisation; semidirect product with the unipotent radical of the Borel

ideas.what: Monomorphism into a product of structural groups and characters (chi, eps_2, eps_3), with the image cut out by determinant and sign equations
ideas.modern_name: explicit equations of a closed subgroup scheme

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an explicit group scheme over Z (M_{rho,sigma}, SM_{rho,sigma} ≅ SΣ*) as the linear/congruence-level receptacle of the genus-1 loop equation. He states canonical maps from the Teichmüller-tower group M~_{0,3} into its Ẑ-points modulo Σ. The literature studies the GT action on SL2(Ẑ), but not, as far as I know, this specific Z-group-scheme model with the order-6/order-4 elliptic data and the eps_1^{mu-1} cusp twist.
missed.quote: alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} = eps beta sigma(beta)^{-1} eps_1(mu-1)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a concrete 'abelianised/linear' test object for the genus-1 GT groups (Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps, Enriquez's elliptic GT). Its value is mainly historical: it documents that Grothendieck formulated a genus-1 loop equation with the cyclotomic twist at the cusp.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly careful bookkeeping (embeddings, characters, a change of coordinates). Its interest is historical: an explicit genus-1, matrix-level version of the GT loop equation with the cusp exponent mu. Mathematically, the GL2-level content is elementary and the genus-1 GT relations are now known from other authors.
transcription_corrections: (15): the image reads B'_0 (not B'_rho). By consistency with page 478 (2), the next factor should be T_rho, though the hand may have written T_sigma. The fourth factor is G (underlined), not 'B_sigma[?]'.
(16): 'b(sigma) = eps(sigma)' should be read as b(sigma) = eps·sigma, i.e. as in the manuscript, with a slip by Grothendieck.
(17): '^ℓG' is a stray mark; the target is G x G x G x G_m x mu_2.
(14): the bracket under 'sigma(b)' reads (t b)^{-1}, i.e. transpose-inverse.
'donnés dans la définition (A) B)' probably refers to definitions (1),(3) of the previous page; 'on complète par' is confirmed.
